plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: Leafless stems shoot up overnight, each topped with a burst of crimson flowers. The long, curling stamens give the blooms a spidery, firework-like look. They light up rice-field edges, riverbanks and temple grounds in glowing red ribbons.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-September to early October, peaking around the autumn equinox
plants.location: Japan, especially the rice-paddy margins and riverbanks of Honshu
plants.funFact: The flowers appear before the leaves. The foliage emerges after the blooms fade and persists through winter. In Japan the flower is tied to the autumn equinox holiday, Higan.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac-pink goblets rise straight from bare soil in damp meadows and woodland edges. They look like crocuses blooming out of season. The leaves appeared months earlier in spring and have since died away.
plants.location: Meadows and open woodland across central and western Europe, including the UK, Germany and France
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it isn't a true crocus. It is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine, and every part of the plant is highly toxic.

plants.name: Dimorphotheca sinuata
plants.description: Sun-seeking daisies turn the dry landscape into a carpet of glowing orange. The petals have dark, metallic-looking centers and open wide in bright sunshine, then close up on cloudy days and at night.
plants.bloomingSeason: August to September, as the southern hemisphere spring peaks
plants.location: Namaqualand and the Western and Northern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The flower heads follow the sun and stay shut when it is overcast. Because of this, the wildflower displays are best seen on clear, sunny midday afternoons.
